gate_adjudication.conclusion: A guard tube is a PREDICTION of a gate refusal, and on the one case tested end to end the prediction was CORRECT.  The correct reading of this file is therefore NOT 'the guard costs two edges' -- it is 'the guard hides two proposals, and at least one of them the gate refuses anyway'.  The pre-filter is still worth challenging per-net, because it is cheap to and the gate remains the authority, but the default assumption should be that it is right.
gate_adjudication.note: THE PRE-FILTER'S TWO 'COSTS' WERE PUT THROUGH THE REAL GATE, and the first one is not a cost at all.  `route_maze_batch.py /I2C_SCL_INT /I2C_SDA_INT --partial --repair-planes` WITHOUT `--guard`.

interpretation: THE GUARD IS A PRE-FILTER, NOT THE AUTHORITY.  It exists so the proposer does not waste a transaction on copper the gate would refuse for severing a pour bond.  But clause 4 of `route_maze_batch.py` already measures whole-board retained open edges after the real refill AND after the `--repair-planes` stitch, so a route that slots a pour is either re-bonded by a barrel or REFUSED on the numbers.  Dropping the pre-filter for a named net therefore weakens nothing: it only lets the gate judge a proposal the pre-filter would have hidden.  It does NOT follow that the guard should be dropped in general -- it is cheap and it is right about 7 of these 9 nets -- only that a net it blocks deserves a guarded-OFF run through the FULL gate with `--repair-planes` before being called a wall.
note: READ-ONLY A/B of the POUR-BOND GUARD's routing cost.  The guard exists to keep every net OTHER than a tube's own out of the copper that is the only bond between a pour pad and its island, and every promotion since D-585 has carried it.  Nothing had ever measured what it COSTS.  Each of the nine open retained nets below was offered every MST edge twice on the same board, at its own contract, with `maze3d.Field(guard=...)` OFF and ON -- 311 guarded F.Cu cells and 1168 guarded B.Cu cells.  The answer is small and exact.
